assertions: A record whose only defect is its version holds the unit back with its bytes intact, and the identical record at the current version still fast-forwards.
The hold-back names the schema and the change, and does NOT say "locally modified".
A clone re-baselines a record it cannot read and leaves one it can.
A stale CHECKOUT record still keeps the unit a checkout.

evidence.mutation: Removed the schema gate (usableAsEvidence -> `record != null`, 1 definition site feeding 3 readers, counted first): killed "a record from an older schema is not a licence to replace anything" ON THE BYTES -- the destination was overwritten -- and "a clone re-baselines a record it cannot read". Silenced staleSchemaNote (1 site): killed the same test on the message, which then fell back to the #43 sentence about "no materialization record of its own" -- true, and useless to whoever has to act on it. Gated `mode` on the version too (1 site added): killed "a record this build cannot read still keeps a checkout a checkout" -- the record came back as mode COPY, the checkout demoted to an ordinary copy. Removed the deliberate clone re-baseline (1 site): killed "a clone re-baselines a record it cannot read". Every mutation reverted; shasum -a 256 -c OK.
evidence.note: The insensitive first version of the checkout assertion never landed -- it was written and replaced inside the same session, so `git show --stat -- src/test` on the first commit is 673 insertions and ZERO deletions. No coverage was lost; an earlier report described it as a deletion, which the diff does not say. A first version of the checkout assertion, written against a non-git child tree, was INSENSITIVE to the mode mutation -- the stale record also fails as a COPY baseline, so the unit was held back either way and the test passed for the wrong reason. Replaced with the git-backed form, where the child tree is byte-identical to the store's and the demotion is reachable through the adopt-an-identical-copy branch. A mutation that kills nothing is a finding about the test.
unit: HomeSyncTest "a record from an older schema is not a licence to replace anything" -- on the destination's bytes, its tree digest, and both surfaces' wording, with the current-schema half asserted too
HomeSyncTest "a clone re-baselines a record it cannot read, and leaves one it can"
HomeSyncGitUnitTest "a record this build cannot read still keeps a checkout a checkout" -- on the record's own bytes

ticket.model_change: NONE, and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming. A record whose schema this build cannot read is exactly RecordlessSyncRecord -- every path claims NoBaseline -- which External.tla has had since #43, and AReconciliationOnlyWritesAgainstABaselineBothHomesPassedThrough is already the property that such a record may not license a write. Adding a schema dimension would state the same rule twice, which planning_rules.dual_representation_rule forbids for the same reason.
ticket.objective: #41 changed what a materialization record's digests are computed OVER: re-derivable build output stopped counting as unit content. The version number did not move, so a record written before it and one written after describe two different trees and are not comparable. The first pass over a home holding a pre-#41 record therefore saw a mismatch it could not explain and held the unit back -- correctly, and SILENTLY. All seven onboarded constituent homes carry such records. The silence is the defect, not the hold-back.
ticket.resolution: Both halves of the issue's "either/or", because they answer different questions. BUMP: RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION is 2, and usableAsEvidence -- one definition, three readers (copyBaseline, hasEntries, sourceHeldTheseBytes: exactly the three showings the baseline rule accepts) -- makes any other version no evidence at all. Under the baseline rule that costs exactly the ability to fast-forward and cannot cost bytes. The OTHER reading of "re-baseline" -- recomputing contentDigest from whatever the destination currently holds so the tree reads as untouched again -- is the unsafe one: true by construction, proving nothing about whether an agent edited the unit since the copy, and a licence for the next reconcile. That is CHM-9's shape reached through the version field. `mode` is deliberately NOT gated on the version. It is the one field whose whole job is to stop a deletion: a project-wide COPY default that won over a recorded CHECKOUT would demote a tree holding unpushed commits. Deliberate re-baselining happens in the one place it is sound -- recordCloneBaselines, where the home's content IS what the home it was copied from held, by construction. Elsewhere a pristine unit self-heals on the next pass and a non-pristine one holds back. MESSAGE: staleSchemaNote names the schema and issue #41 as the cause, on all three surfaces that report a hold-back (home sync's detail, which close-out renders; copyUnit's held-back detail; and locallyModifiedUnits, the predicate a prune and a teardown consult).
